items.title: Andrew Morgan Interview, 1961-07-04
items.q: I'd taken lessons with him through the auto language on a clarinet.

ctx.x: Well, I was going to ask some more about your lessons, um, because naturally we're interested in some of these real old timers like Chaline and I didn't get, never, we'll never get to talk to him of course. Old man Chaline? Yeah, anything that you can tell us about your lessons? Did he use a regular method book? Do you remember what it was?
Well, yeah, we used to use, uh, an auto language at that time, you see. And I'd taken lessons with him through the auto language on a clarinet.

items.title: Andrew Morgan Interview, 1961-07-04
items.q: him and I used to sit down and play duets together.

ctx.x: I was going to ask about Chalney again. Somebody told me, maybe it was Harold Dejan, I think, took some lessons from him. Or what's it, Brother Cornbread or something, you know, the clarinetist.
Well, Brother Cornbread used to take lessons with old man Chalney. Him and I was a scholar over there, because he had a very large place, and he had just so many youngsters.
Maybe he said he had a band, didn't he?
